SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE - NOT A REAL PAPER
Lottery Days and the Cross-Section: A Fake Study
A. Placeholder and B. Example (2099)

Abstract
This fabricated note exists only to test the extraction pipeline. We sort stocks
by their maximum daily return in the previous month and find that stocks with ex-
treme positive daily returns earn lower future returns. Investors who like lottery-
like payoffs overpay for these stocks, so their subsequent returns are low.
No real data were used; every number below is invented for testing.

1. Data and method
Our sample contains all common stocks in the Imaginary Exchange with a price of at
least $5. We use daily stock returns only.
At the end of each month we compute MAX, the largest single-day return of each stock
during that month, and sort stocks into ten equal-count deciles on MAX.
Portfolios are held for one month and rebalanced monthly, with no skip between the
formation month and the holding month.
We form value-weighted decile portfolios, weighting each stock by its market capitalization.
MAX_{i,t} = max(R_{i,d}), d = 1, ..., D_t

2. Results
Table 1 reports the decile portfolios. The lowest MAX decile earns the highest
return, and the highest MAX decile earns the lowest return.
The return difference between decile 10 and decile 1 is -0.99% per month (made up).
We therefore expect the low-MAX decile to outperform the high-MAX decile.
We do not state whether a minimum number of trading days is required in the month.
